judgement_calls.title: opening_excluded re-implements kSeededFaClient's enrol-and-chart prefix instead of sharing it
judgement_calls.evidence: New cell (fixed-asset-acquisition.test.mjs): `const w = await faWorld(); const o = await wb.onboardingClient(w.users.hana, "884refuse"); await wb.seedOpeningCoa(w.users.alice, o.client); await buildFaChart(w.users.alice, o.client); await upsertFaProfile(w.users.alice, { client: o.client, assetAccount: COST, accumAccount: ACCUM, expenseAccount: EXPENSE });` is, line for line, the same shape as the first five lines of the existing `kSeededFaClient` in x41-fa-world.mjs:370-374: `const w = await faWorld(); const o = await wb.onboardingClient(w.users.hana, \`x41k_${label}_${uniqTag()}\`); await wb.seedOpeningCoa(w.users.alice, o.client); await buildFaChart(w.users.alice, o.client); await upsertFaProfile(w.users.alice, { client: o.client, assetAccount: COST, accumAccount: ACCUM, expenseAccount: EXPENSE });` — the only difference is the client label.
judgement_calls.why_it_matters: The two call sites are now two independent sources of truth for 'what does an enrolled FA onboarding client look like'; a future change to enrolment (e.g. a new required profile field) has to be made in both places or the new cell silently drifts from the fixture kSeededFaClient's own callers already rely on.
judgement_calls.suggested_fix: Extract the shared prefix into its own exported helper in x41-fa-world.mjs (e.g. freshEnrolledFaClient(label) returning { w, o }) and have both kSeededFaClient and p639.birth.opening_excluded call it.
judgement_calls.note: Judgement call per the code-review skill's Fowler baseline, not a documented-standard breach; no repo standard endorses or forbids this duplication.

judgement_calls.title: forceOpenedAt duplicates backdateStatus's trigger-disable idiom instead of generalizing it
judgement_calls.evidence: New local helper: `async function forceOpenedAt(intent, isoTimestamp) { await rootQuery("alter table clara.checkout_intents disable trigger t_checkout_intents_session_stamp"); try { await rootQuery("update clara.checkout_intents set opened_at=$2 where id=$1", [intent, isoTimestamp]); } finally { await rootQuery("alter table clara.checkout_intents enable trigger t_checkout_intents_session_stamp"); } }` is structurally identical to the pre-existing, exported `backdateStatus` in checkout-convergence-fixtures.mjs:253-262 (same disable/try/update/finally-enable shape against the same trigger, a different column). The new function's own comment even names backdateStatus as the idiom it mirrors.
judgement_calls.why_it_matters: The disable/re-arm dance around t_checkout_intents_session_stamp is now defined twice, once shared (checkout-convergence-fixtures.mjs, exported, reusable) and once private to operator-support.test.mjs; a third file needing to force a different column on the same table would be tempted to paste a third copy rather than reuse one place.
judgement_calls.suggested_fix: Generalize backdateStatus into a small `withSessionStampDisabled(fn)` or `forceColumn(intent, column, value)` helper exported from checkout-convergence-fixtures.mjs, and have forceOpenedAt (and backdateStatus) call it, instead of a new private near-copy in the test file.
judgement_calls.note: Judgement call, not a documented-standard breach — the repo already tolerates this exact shape once (backdateStatus itself); this is the second instance of it.

judgement_calls.title: the guardedReset wrap is the same two-line insertion repeated near-identically in 13 files
judgement_calls.evidence: e.g. hrd-a-recut-guard.test.mjs: `const { reset } = await import("../scripts/reset.mjs"); const { guardedReset } = await import("./rig-reset-guard.mjs"); const { migrate } = await import("../scripts/migrate.mjs"); await guardedReset(reset, { log: () => {} });` — the same `const { guardedReset } = await import(...)` + `guardedReset(reset, ...)` pair appears essentially verbatim 13 times across this diff.
judgement_calls.why_it_matters: A future rename of rig-reset-guard.mjs's export, or a change to what a caller must pass, is a 13-site shotgun edit rather than a one-place change; the drift-guard test this same ticket adds (reset-gate-routing.test.mjs) exists specifically because this kind of scattered per-file duplication is easy to leave inconsistent.
judgement_calls.suggested_fix: A shared `guardedFreshReset()`-style re-export (one place obtains both reset and guardedReset and returns the wrapped callable) would collapse the 13 duplicated import pairs to one definition, at the cost of one more indirection.
judgement_calls.note: The ticket's own Agent Brief (#845, 'Key interfaces') explicitly prescribes this exact per-file shape ('Each upgrade-drill test or kit module: its direct reset({...}) becomes guardedReset(reset, {...})'), so this is a low-priority observation, not something the diff got wrong relative to its own spec — flagged only because the Fowler baseline applies even where a spec is silent on style, and here the spec itself chose the scattered shape.

judgement_calls.title: new os.19 heading breaks the file's own heading convention

judgement_calls.suggested_fix: e.g. `## \`operator-support.test.mjs\` — #844 (cell \`os.19\`)` to match the file's own established heading shape.

test_quality_notes.title: acceptance-2 substitutes a non-delegating spy for scripts/reset.mjs's real export — checked against mocking.md and found justified, not a violation
test_quality_notes.evidence: reset-gate-routing.test.mjs's acceptance-2 cell fetches the real `reset` export only to assert `typeof realReset === "function"`, then calls `guardedReset(wrapped, { log: () => {} })` with `wrapped = async () => { spy.entered += 1; }` standing in for it.
test_quality_notes.assessment: mocking.md says 'don't mock ... anything you control', which this could look like on its face (scripts/reset.mjs is repo-owned). Two things clear it: (1) guardedReset(fn, options) takes its destructive callback as an injected parameter by design — substituting a benign callback to unit-test the guard's own refuse-before-invoke behaviour is exactly mocking.md's own dependency-injection guidance, not mocking an internal collaborator to shortcut a real assertion; (2) RIG.md forbids ever setting CLARA_RIG_ALLOW_RESET on this shared rig, so exercising the actual DROP SCHEMA path here is not an option this suite has — the destructive reset() is the closest thing this test has to a system boundary. The exact same non-delegating-spy shape already exists for T19 in rig-reset-guard.test.mjs; this cell was reviewed and fixed in fix round 1 (L03-S1) specifically to match that established precedent (it originally delegated to the real export, which the SPEC review correctly flagged as dangerous; the fix removed the delegation). No further action needed on the STANDARDS axis.

summary: No hard violations of a documented repo standard found in this diff (packages/db/tests/** only, 6 commits, tickets #845/#844/#884). The four findings are all Fowler-baseline judgement calls, all minor-or-note: three instances of Duplicated Code (a new fixed-asset cell re-deriving kSeededFaClient's enrolment prefix instead of sharing it; a new forceOpenedAt helper duplicating the existing backdateStatus trigger-disable idiom instead of generalizing it; the guardedReset wrap repeated near-identically across 13 files, though that shape is what #845's own Agent Brief prescribes) and one cosmetic README heading inconsistency. On TEST QUALITY against /tdd: the one test double in the diff (reset-gate-routing.test.mjs's non-delegating spy standing in for scripts/reset.mjs) was checked against mocking.md and judged justified — it substitutes a callback into a higher-order guard function by design (dependency injection), mirrors an already-established repo idiom (T19's own spy in rig-reset-guard.test.mjs), and is the only safe way to prove a refuse-before-run guarantee given RIG.md's standing prohibition on ever exercising the real destructive path on this shared rig; it was also independently re-verified non-delegating by the SPEC-axis recheck already on file. No tautological expectations were found (every new assertion's expected value is either a fixture-supplied literal or a cross-check against a second, independent read, never a recomputation of the code's own formula). No evidence of horizontal slicing in git log --stat. The repo's own documented persona-discipline standard for fixed-asset-acquisition.test.mjs (README.md:52-53) is honoured by both new #884 cells, and reset-gate-routing.test.mjs's source-scanning structural cells match an established repo drift-guard convention rather than inventing a new anti-pattern seam. Nothing here blocks acceptance; the four findings are optional cleanups, not required fixes.
